findings.description: The new Bash matcher drops case-insensitive detection even for explicit hidden path tokens. For example, `cat /tmp/Hidden/tests.json` matches neither uppercase HIDDEN nor lowercase hidden, and /tmp is an allowed root.
findings.failure_mode: A transcript accessing hidden material through a mixed-case path is graded as uncontaminated, whereas the previous lowercase substring check detected it.
findings.suggested_fix: Match the path-token alternatives case-insensitively while preserving the intended exemption for bare English prose; add mixed-case path regression cases.

findings.description: The unconditional quoted-prefix exemption bypasses the explicit host-mode home restriction. With `cat "$HOME"/private/credentials`, HOME_WORD misses the intervening quote, and after_closing_quote causes the remaining /private/credentials candidate to be discarded.
findings.failure_mode: A common shell spelling for accessing files outside the host sandbox is now graded as uncontaminated. Previously, the absolute suffix triggered outside_path.
findings.suggested_fix: Recognize quoted HOME expansions before discarding path tails and classify them as outside_path in host mode. Cover both "$HOME"/… and "${HOME}"/….

findings.description: The HEREDOC pattern consumes `[^\n]*\n` after the delimiter word, i.e. the whole remainder of the opener line, and strip_heredocs replaces the entire match with `<<HEREDOC`. Anything that follows the `<<WORD` token on the same line (a redirect target, a pipe to tee, a second argument) is removed before the ABS_WORD path scan runs. `cat <<'EOF' > /root/.bashrc`, `cat <<EOF | tee /home/operator/notes.txt`, `python3 - <<'PY' > /srv/out.json` are all stripped to `cat <<HEREDOC`, so the outside path is never seen. Before 1.2.2 these words were path candidates and `/root/...` was a contamination hit; DEC-0541 only intended to exempt the written body text.
findings.failure_mode: An agent that writes a file outside the sandbox with the most common heredoc idiom (`cat <<'EOF' > /outside/path`) is not flagged `contaminated`; the run stays in the scored set.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip only the body: after locating the opener, keep the rest of the opener line and remove from the following line through the terminator line. E.g. a line-based pass: for each line containing a `<<[-]?['"]?WORD` token, emit the line unchanged, then skip lines until one equals WORD (after optional leading tabs for `<<-`). Add a test with `cat <<'EOF' > /root/x` asserting contamination.

findings.description: Confirming the primary reviewer's finding 1 with the mechanism: the body group `(?:.*?\n)*?` is compiled with re.S, so `.` matches newlines and each `.*?\n` may span any number of lines. When the terminator `\2` never appears, the engine tries every partition of the k newlines into segments: 2^(k-1) attempts. The opener also matches non-heredoc text: a here-string `<<<'X'` (the regex re-anchors at the second `<`), a C/Python shift `a <<b`, or an unterminated heredoc. Any such Bash tool_use with ~30 lines makes check_value run for minutes to hours. check_value runs inside grade() for every events-*.jsonl record, so the whole grade hangs.
findings.failure_mode: A single transcript with `<<` plus tens of newlines and no terminator stalls ablation-grade.sh indefinitely; the batch runner's post_run never returns for that trial and the batch stops progressing without a watchdog (the pipeline process group is already gone).
findings.suggested_fix: Drop re.S and make the body line-anchored: `(?:[^\n]*\n)*?` with the terminator matched as `^[ \t]*\2[ \t]*$` under re.M; or replace the regex with the line-based parser suggested in DISS-001. Add a bats case with `cat <<EOF` followed by 60 lines and no EOF, asserting the grade completes in under a second.

findings.description: The header still says `hidden` is matched in any case, and before this change `"hidden" in val.lower()` did so for every tool. HIDDEN_TOKEN is compiled without re.I; only the all-caps alternative `HIDDEN` is case-insensitive in effect. In a Bash command, `ls tests/Hidden/`, `cat Hidden_tests.py`, `ls hidden_Tests` (lowercase, fine) vs `ls HiddenTests` (missed) now depend on capitalisation. Separately, the token shapes have no glob-adjacent form: `find . -name '*hidden*'`, `ls hidden*`, `grep -rl hidden* .` have `hidden` next to `*` or `'`, which is neither in the lookbehind nor the lookahead class, so an explicit search for hidden test files is not a hit. These are command tokens, not the prose case DEC-0551 set out to exempt.
findings.failure_mode: An agent probing for the hidden test tree with a mixed-case name or a glob is not flagged `contaminated`; its run is scored.
findings.suggested_fix: Compile HIDDEN_TOKEN with re.I (drop the separate `HIDDEN` branch) and add `*` and `?` to the adjacency classes: `(?<=[/._=*?-])hidden\b|\bhidden(?=[/_=*?-]|\.[A-Za-z0-9])`. Add tests for `ls tests/Hidden/` and `find . -name '*hidden*'`.

findings.description: after_closing_quote treats any `/x/y` glued to a closing quote as a path tail. HOME_WORD only matches `$HOME/` with the slash immediately after the variable, so `cat "$HOME"/Documents/secret` or `ls "${HOME}"/.aws` matches neither HOME_WORD nor (now) ABS_WORD: the `/Documents/secret` word is skipped at line 1442. Before 1.2.5 that word was a candidate and, in host mode, an outside hit. Python literal prefixes have the same shape: `python3 -c 'open(f"/root/x")'` or `r"/root/x"` put a letter at pos-2, so the path is skipped.
findings.failure_mode: Host-mode runs that read the operator's home via a quoted `$HOME` or a Python literal with a prefix are not flagged.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend HOME_WORD to accept an optional closing quote: `(?:~|\$HOME|\$\{HOME\})['"]?/`. In after_closing_quote, only treat the quote as closing a token when the quote is balanced for the preceding word (e.g. the previous word contains a matching opening quote), or restrict the exemption to `"$VAR"/` and `'...'/` shapes where the character before the opening quote is a path/identifier character.

findings.description: in_quotes decides by raw quote parity over the whole prefix, ignoring quote nesting and escapes. An apostrophe inside a double-quoted string earlier in the command flips the parity: `git commit -m "don't break" && ls /root` or `echo "it's done"; ls -la /home` sees one `'` before `/root`, so the one-component sensitive word is treated as pattern text and skipped at line 1444. Commit messages and echo text with apostrophes are common in agent commands.
findings.failure_mode: `ls /root`, `ls /home`, `ls /mnt` after any text containing an apostrophe are not flagged.
findings.suggested_fix: Track quote state properly: walk the prefix once, toggling single/double state only when the quote is not inside the other kind and not backslash-escaped. Or use shlex-like tokenisation of the body and check whether the matched word is inside a quoted token.

findings.description: The one-component rule (line 1423) now skips every `/word` that is not root, home, mnt, media or srv. Real data-holding single components exist outside that set: `/Users` and `/private` on a macOS host, `/data`, `/export`, `/boot`, `/run`, `/snap`, `/flag`. `ls /Users`, `ls -la /data` were outside hits before 1.2.1 and are now silent. Host mode (allowed with LOA_EVAL_ALLOW_HOST_GRADING=1) is where `/Users` matters.
findings.failure_mode: A one-component directory listing outside the sandbox is not flagged unless it names one of five Linux directories.
findings.suggested_fix: Invert the rule: skip a one-component word only when it looks like a Loa slash command or a regex delimiter (lowercase-with-hyphen command names present in .claude/commands, or a `/x/` with a preceding s/y/=/~/quote), and keep every other one-component absolute word as a candidate. At minimum add Users, private, data, export, boot, run to SENSITIVE_SINGLE.

findings.description: Confirming the primary reviewer's finding 4: the `/.` skip runs on the raw word before os.path.normpath (which outside() applies later). `cat /./root/x`, `ls /../home/operator`, `/.//root/x` all begin with `/.` and are skipped, although normpath resolves them to `/root/x` and `/home/operator`. The intent (root dot-directories such as `/.claude/...`) only needs the first component itself to be a dot-name.
findings.failure_mode: A path written with a leading `/./` or `/../` escapes the outside check.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise first: `n = os.path.normpath(w)`; skip only when `re.match(r'^/\.[^/]', n)`; feed `n` to cands. Likewise apply the `=` exemption only when `=` appears in a component other than the last, or drop it in favour of a sed-specific check.
